## The decision for today

What object are we constructing, what information does it retain, and what scientific claim could it support?


[Lecture walkthrough](solutions.ipynb)

---

## Story

Week 5 is the first practical week. The aim is not just to compute
persistence, but to choose a construction appropriate to the data
object. The data object comes first; the complex follows.

---

## Method map

- Point cloud with coordinates: alpha or Rips complexes.

- Pairwise distances only: Vietoris–Rips complexes.

---

## Computational cautions

Rips complexes grow quickly. For an $N$-point cloud, the Vietoris–Rips
filtration contains $O(N^2)$ edges, $O(N^3)$ triangles, $O(N^4)$
tetrahedra and so on. Even when truncating at dimension 2, the size can
scale like $O(N^3)$. This is why the choice of maximum dimension,
maximum filtration value and sparsification strategy is not merely
technical.

---

## Examples

Use a noisy circle versus noisy disk as a sanity check. Use an annulus
with uneven sampling to show that persistence is not immune to sampling
effects. Use a greyscale image to introduce lower-star or cubical
persistence. Use a small weighted graph to ask whether pairwise cycles
or clique-complex holes are the object of interest.

---

## One stack, three objects

![](../../assets/week05-data-constructions.svg){fig-alt="Point cloud, weighted graph and scalar grid mapped to three different filtered constructions." height="210"}

| Input | Construction | Filtration value |
|---|---|---|
| Point cloud | Rips complex | Distance threshold |
| Weighted graph | Graph or clique complex | Edge weight |
| Scalar grid | Cubical complex | Cell value |

The common software does not make these the same mathematical object.

---

## Where do the scalar values live?

Lower star: values begin on vertices.

Cubical practical: values begin on top-dimensional grid cells.

State the convention before interpreting birth.

Alpha complexes are optional, not part of the core practical.

---

## Sensitivity or a new question?

Subsample the same point cloud: sensitivity check.

Fill graph cliques: new higher-order assumption.

Negate a scalar field: switch from low-valued to high-valued structure.

::: {.sticking}
**▶ Likely sticking point.** Not every software setting is a harmless tuning parameter.
:::

---

## Computational reporting

State observation and simplex counts, maximum dimension and threshold,
coefficient field, sparsification, runtime and memory failures.

---

## DP relevance

Static persistence is not claiming that a dynamical system is static. It
freezes one representation: a time window, a state cloud, a snapshot, an
interaction graph or a scalar field. This is the lowest-risk baseline.
If a single topological snapshot cannot distinguish regimes or
performance-relevant states, then more sophisticated dynamic topology
needs stronger justification.
